title: Workload Muse: continuous profiling and cautious batching policy applier
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a recommendation engine (codename: Workload Muse) that continuously profiles live request streams and suggests batching + caching parameter updates safe to apply automatically or via a staged rollout. Focus on workload fingerprinting, lightweight heuristics for merge-window and max-batch-size, KV cache retention tuning, and a conservative apply/rollback controller.
acceptance_criteria: Muse collects per-route profiling data (prefix length distribution, arrival interarrival times, kv-cache hit rate, observed sequence lengths) for at least 14 days of production traffic without added tail latency > 5%.
Muse produces a per-route recommendation payload: {recommended_max_batch, merge_window_ms, kv_cache_ttl_ms, expected_cost_delta_pct, confidence_score} (confidence_score is 0-100).

Safe-apply controller can perform shadow-canary and gradual ramp (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) and automatically rollback if latency p95 increases > 10ms or error-rate increases > 0.3% relative to baseline.
A/B and cost-savings dashboard cards available in Console for routes with Muse-applied changes and expected vs actual cost delta recorded.
Unit and e2e tests cover heuristic edge cases (high-entropy short prompts, long-chat multi-turn sessions, bursty microburst patterns).
technical_notes: Profiling pipeline: nginx -> eyeball-proxy middleware -> kafka topic 'muse-profiles' -> lightweight aggregator (1s tumbling windows) -> clickhouse for retention analytics.

Fingerprint features: median_tokens, 90th_seq_len, interarrival_p95_ms, prefix_commonality_score (Jaccard of first 32 tokens per route), kv_cache_hit_rate, is_chat_session (bool), downstream_model_family.

Heuristics: if prefix_commonality_score > 0.6 and median_tokens < 64 then recommend larger merge_window_ms (40-100ms depending on microburst rate). If kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.35 and steady-state session_count_high then increase kv_cache_ttl_ms up to 60k ms with fallback rules.
Confidence model: simple rule-weighted score initially; plan to augment with logistic regression on historical success features (cost saved, latency delta).
Safety controls: global kill-switch, per-customer opt-out flag, per-route whitelist/blacklist, maximum allowed expected cost saving threshold before requiring manual approval (>40% must be manual).
Persistence: recommendation objects stored as JSON in phoenix-store with versioning to support rollbacks and audit trail.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Experiments (shadow-only): Run Muse recommendations in shadow mode for 2 weeks on 5 low-risk routes. Compare expected vs observed metrics.
Phase 1 - Canary applies: Automated apply to 10% traffic with strict circuit-breaker checks for p95 latency and error-rate for 72h.
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days with continuous monitoring and automated rollback triggers.
Phase 3 - Broad rollout: After 30 days of stable results, enable Muse as an opt-in advisory for all customers and permit auto-apply for internal Redwood routes.
Rollback: Immediate rollback path documented in runbook; recommendation versions retained so revert is a single API call.
telemetry_checks: Baseline queries (ClickHouse): median(tokens) and p95 latency per route over last 7d.
Cost check: token_cost_per_minute and request_count deltas; ensure cost reduction estimate matches observed within 20% after 48h.
Safety signals: p95_latency_delta_pct, error_rate_delta_pct, tail_queue_time_ms. Thresholds: p95_latency_delta_pct > 5% OR error_rate_delta_pct > 0.2% -> mark unhealthy.
KV cache sanity: if kv_cache_hit_rate falls > 10 percentage points after apply, trigger rollback and create incident ticket automatically.
Observability: emit recommendation.metrics.{expected_cost_delta,applied,rolled_back,confidence} to metrics pipeline and annotate all changes in Console.
